abandon: The board already contradicts m06's core claim that the cued base loses its hold on the givens late in long answers, so that its gap to RL grows with position even on problems it has started correctly. (1) The prefix hand-off test measures this directly, and the base continuing late in an answer is as good as RL. result-a6ab7a: 'RL's advantage is in the first half of the answer and is in the text by the halfway point', 'Right prefixes from 50 % on: both finish equally (83 vs 83 of 88 base prefixes; 131 vs 134 of 140 RL prefixes)', and 'Refuted: 'late checking' (no RL edge at 75 %)'. From a sound prefix at 50 % or more, the base finishes as often as RL, and the base finishing RL's 75 % prefix recovers 17.5 of 21.3 points. If the givens faded with distance, the base would be the weaker finisher exactly in these late segments. (2) The observation m06 starts from, 'the gap rises with length even where neither model hits the cap', is not in the item it cites. knowledge-9e4147 says 'T1 cap hits exceed T2's by 15.2 points in Q4 and by 0-1.6 elsewhere'. So 15.2 of the 20.0-point Q4 gap is cap hits, and the finished-answer gap in Q4 (about 5 points) is smaller than in Q1-Q3 (about 9 to 14). (3) Wrong steps sit early, not late. result-afc423: 'First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer'. result-c495fe: 'before a judged misreading it has already lost 32 points', so misreadings are set up early in the text. result-f3d708: 'misread samples do not have the lowest value' of problem dependence. A late drift of the givens predicts the opposite in each case.
